prompts:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a DESIGN EXPLORATION DRAWING of a pirate redesign of Freelancer's Rheinland rh_elite, respecting the actual supplied source game's visual language.
Input image roles: Image 1 is the existing 3D ship to redesign, and is the mandatory exact cockpit-shape reference. Images 2 and 3 are the original Rheinland concept art and family grammar. Image 4 provides stepped heavy armor, visible mechanical joints and engineered equipment mounting references, NOT its weapons. Image 5 is the player's animated rh_alt_elite: understand the split hinged short panels, not a copied airframe.
The user rejected a flat wide conventional jet with swept delta wings and twin aircraft tail fins. The new drawing must belong to the ORIGINAL RH family by silhouette: distinct forward cockpit head, a visibly narrow neck behind it, deep vertically developed stepped armored central/rear body, dominant upright circular mechanical masses enclosed in angular armor, short thick articulated appendages and compact cylindrical engine pods. Strong simple large forms and readable joints before small surface details.
CRITICAL INVARIANT: preserve Image 1's actual cockpit module: same blunt rounded/trapezoid cabin nose, same large dark blue front and side glazing, same wraparound metal lower chin and narrow black/yellow window-frame trim, same shape and scale. Do not substitute a pointed fighter jet canopy, a glass bubble, or the cockpit from the historical sketches. The rest of the craft may change substantially.
Weapons are separate interchangeable game models. Draw NO guns, NO barrels, NO missiles, NO turrets built into the hull, and NO firing effects. Show only a few EMPTY compact weapon mounting pads with mounting sockets and plausible clearance for later separate equipment. Distinguish empty hardpoint pads from engine exhausts. Do not copy mounted weapons from the reference art.
Style/medium: early-2000s industrial science-fiction game concept sheet, careful dark graphite construction lines, restrained gray/olive metal marker shading with small worn burgundy replacement plates, white/off-white paper. Clearly drawn bevels, round housings, broad calm metal plates, a few purposeful vents. Enough detail for a 3D modeller, no dense decorative greeble noise. No scene, no stars, no cinematic glow. Clean, utilitarian, slightly worn pirate refit. No skull/cross insignia needed.
Composition: landscape design sheet with one dominant three-quarter view (nose toward lower right, rear toward upper left, all parts inside frame), one smaller consistent SIDE view and one small diagram showing the SAME wing panels in their folded pose. The three views must describe the same coherent craft, not three different ships. The upright drum is longitudinally oriented as in the source, NOT a horizontal flying saucer and NOT a hoop around the entire ship. Leave visible white space between views. This is a sketch, not a screenshot or final production asset.
VARIANT A — segmented armored drum. Redesign the original single big upright aft disk into a thicker layered mechanical drum, with an angular stepped outer rim divided into three broad fitted armor sectors and a clearly recessed circular inner face with a few broad horizontal louvers. Retain the tall narrow body/head/neck relationship of the original, while reshaping the central body into two substantial sloped armor shoulders around the spine. Lower compact barrel engine housings carry short two-piece thick wing paddles on visible pivots, with squared/beveled ends and a split between the panels. Their folding diagram shows the paddles rotating upright alongside the body while retaining equipment space. Pirate character comes from deliberate reinforcement braces and several mismatched armor sectors, not spikes or excessive rust. Do not just trace the old model with minor tip changes: change the central armor construction and rear drum profile visibly while preserving the family silhouette. Only text: "RH / A".
